title: Organophosphorus and Carbamate Compounds Poisoning
tocPath: APPROACH TO PATIENTS WITH EMERGENCY CONDITIONS

blocks.text: Organophosphates and carbamates are insecticides that inhibit cholinesterase, causing accumulation of acetylcholine and leading to cholinergic toxicity.

blocks.text: Organophosphates: Malathion, Parathion, TEPP, mevinphos Carbamates: carbaryl, methiocarb
Exposure occurs via ingestion, inhalation, or dermal absorption.
Salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, emesis, bronchorrhea, bronchospasm,
Muscle fasciculations, weakness progressing to paralysis
Pulmonary oedema, respiratory depression, respiratory failure
Immediately remove patient from exposure source.
If dermal exposure: remove clothing and wash skin thoroughly with soap and water.
If ocular exposure: irrigate eyes with clean water or normal saline.
Do NOT induce vomiting (risk of aspiration due to hydrocarbon solvents).
Gastric decontamination (NG aspiration) Consider: NG aspiration ONLY in severe ingestion AND when airway is secured (intubated patient)
Avoid decontamination procedures if airway is not protected due to risk of aspiration and worsening respiratory failure
Monitor: Respiratory rate, Heart rate, Level of consciousness, Chest secretions (auscultation).

Atropine is life-saving and titrated to clinical endpoint (not fixed dose).
Pralidoxime is indicated only in organophosphate poisoning (not carbamates in most cases).
Early airway protection is critical in severe poisoning.
